alternative ways to determine if there are other planets...

At far ditances, there are relatively few. Even then, only large planets can be realistically detected. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methods_of_detecting_exoplanets

For the most part it is either a situation of a large planet transiting between its star and us and we detect it via the dimming and change in light spectrum of the star. Another method is to detect the star moving in a very slight orbit due to the large planet's gravity well acting on the star as it orbits the star. Neither method detects the planet directly though because it simply isn't large enough. Earth sized planets are on the verge of impossible because they have even less of an effect than a large planet.

As for communicating back and forth with Earth from another galaxy, not viable. It isn't a matter of technology but because of the speed of light. Assuming the suggestion of 200 light years distance, a message will take at least that many years to make it from the exoplanet to Earth. A response to the message will take just as long to return. Four hundred years per communication.
